stem: Sound is produced by __________ objects.
solution: Sound is produced by objects that vibrate (move rapidly to and fro).

stem: The rapid to-and-fro motion of an object that produces sound is called __________.
solution: Vibration is the rapid back-and-forth motion of an object that produces sound.

stem: In humans, sound is produced by the __________.
solution: The voice box (larynx) contains vocal cords whose vibrations produce the human voice.

stem: Sound needs a __________ to travel; it cannot travel through a vacuum.
solution: Sound needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel and cannot pass through a vacuum.

stem: Sound travels fastest in __________.
solution: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases, because particles are closest in solids.

stem: The part of the human body that detects sound is the __________.
solution: The ear detects sound and helps us hear.

stem: The thin membrane in the ear that vibrates when sound falls on it is the __________.
solution: The eardrum is a stretched membrane that vibrates when sound reaches it, allowing us to hear.

stem: The number of vibrations (oscillations) per second is called the __________.
solution: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second.

stem: The SI unit of frequency is the __________.
solution: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz); one hertz is one oscillation per second.

stem: The maximum displacement of a vibrating object from its rest position is called the __________.
solution: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of the vibrating object from its central (mean) position.

stem: The time taken to complete one oscillation is called the __________.
solution: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation; it is the inverse of frequency.

stem: The loudness of a sound depends on its __________.
solution: The larger the amplitude of vibration, the louder the sound.

stem: The pitch (shrillness) of a sound depends on its __________.
solution: The higher the frequency, the higher (shriller) the pitch of the sound.

stem: A sound of high frequency has a __________ pitch.
solution: High-frequency sounds have a high, shrill pitch (like a whistle); low-frequency sounds are deep.

stem: The loudness of sound is measured in units called __________.
solution: Loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

stem: Unpleasant or unwanted sound is called __________.
solution: Noise is unpleasant, unwanted sound that can be harmful.

stem: Pleasant sound, such as that produced by musical instruments, is called __________.
solution: Music is pleasant sound, produced for example by musical instruments.

stem: The presence of excessive or unwanted sound in the environment is called __________ pollution.
solution: Noise pollution is the presence of loud, unwanted sound in the environment.

stem: Prolonged exposure to loud noise can cause __________.
options: hearing loss and health problems like stress
solution: Loud noise over long periods can damage hearing and cause stress, headaches and sleeplessness.

stem: The range of frequencies that a normal human can hear is about __________.
solution: Humans can hear sounds in the range of about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz).

stem: Sounds of frequency above 20,000 Hz, which humans cannot hear, are called __________.
solution: Ultrasonic sounds have frequencies above 20 kHz and are inaudible to humans; some animals like dogs and bats can hear them.

stem: Sounds of frequency below 20 Hz, which humans cannot hear, are called __________.
solution: Infrasonic sounds are below 20 Hz and are inaudible to humans.

stem: Which of the following animals can hear ultrasonic sound?
solution: Animals like bats and dogs can hear ultrasonic sounds beyond the human range.

stem: The vocal cords in men are usually __________ than in women, giving men a deeper voice.
solution: Men's vocal cords are longer and thicker, producing a lower-pitched (deeper) voice than women's.

stem: We hear a sound after the object has vibrated because sound takes __________ to travel to our ears.
solution: Sound travels at a finite speed, so it takes some time to reach our ears.

stem: The loudness of a sound __________ as we move away from the source.
solution: Loudness decreases with distance as the sound energy spreads out.

stem: Which of the following would produce a sound of higher pitch?
solution: A tighter, thinner string vibrates at a higher frequency, producing a higher pitch.

stem: In a sitar or guitar, sound is produced by the vibration of __________.
solution: Stringed instruments like the sitar and guitar produce sound through vibrating strings.

stem: In a flute, sound is produced by the vibration of __________.
solution: In wind instruments like the flute, sound is produced by vibrating air columns.

stem: In a drum or tabla, sound is produced by the vibration of __________.
solution: Percussion instruments like drums and tabla produce sound by the vibration of a stretched membrane.

stem: The measures to reduce noise pollution include __________.
options: planting trees, using silencers and limiting loudspeakers
solution: Planting trees (which absorb sound), using silencers, and limiting loudspeakers help reduce noise pollution.

stem: Trees help control noise pollution because they __________.
solution: Trees and plants absorb sound, so planting them along roads reduces noise pollution.

stem: The speed of sound in air is roughly __________.
solution: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air (much slower than light).

stem: Thunder is heard after lightning is seen because __________.
options: sound travels much slower than light
solution: Light travels much faster than sound, so lightning is seen before its thunder is heard.

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum
solution: Sound requires a material medium and cannot travel through a vacuum, unlike light.

stem: An astronaut on the Moon cannot hear another speak directly because __________.
options: there is no air (medium) on the Moon to carry sound
solution: The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so there is no medium to carry sound, and astronauts use radios instead.

stem: A vibrating tuning fork dipped in water splashes the water, showing that it is __________.
solution: The splashing shows that the tuning fork is vibrating, which produces the sound.

stem: Louder sound is produced by a vibrating body with a __________ amplitude.
solution: A larger amplitude of vibration produces a louder sound.

stem: Two sounds of the same loudness but different pitch differ in their __________.
solution: Pitch depends on frequency, so two equally loud sounds of different pitch have different frequencies.

stem: A sound above about 80 dB for long periods can be __________.
solution: Continuous exposure to sounds above about 80 dB can damage hearing and be harmful.

stem: Which of the following pairs a musical instrument with the correct source of its sound?
solution: A guitar produces sound from vibrating strings; a flute uses an air column and a drum a membrane.

stem: People who cannot hear well may use a __________.
solution: A hearing aid amplifies sound to help people with hearing difficulty.

stem: The frequency of a sound determines whether it is __________.
solution: Frequency decides pitch: high frequency gives a shrill sound, low frequency a deep sound.

stem: Which of the following would make sound louder without changing its pitch?
solution: Striking harder increases amplitude and loudness, without changing the frequency (pitch).

stem: A stretched rubber band plucked hard produces a __________ sound than when plucked gently.
solution: Plucking harder gives a larger amplitude and thus a louder sound.

stem: The human ear can be damaged by __________.
options: very loud sounds and inserting sharp objects
solution: Very loud sounds and inserting sharp objects into the ear can damage the delicate eardrum and hearing.

stem: Which medium would carry sound the slowest?
solution: Sound travels slowest in gases like air, because the particles are far apart.

stem: The main difference between noise and music is that music is __________.
options: pleasant and has a regular pattern, while noise is unpleasant
solution: Music is pleasant with a regular pattern; noise is unpleasant and irregular.

stem: To reduce noise from vehicles, horns should be __________.
options: used less and not blown unnecessarily
solution: Minimising unnecessary horn use reduces noise pollution.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Sound' is that:
options: sound is produced by vibrations, needs a medium to travel, and has properties like loudness (amplitude) and pitch (frequency), while excessive noise causes pollution
solution: The chapter explains that sound is produced by vibrations, travels through a medium, and is characterised by loudness and pitch, and that noise pollution is harmful.
